ownershipView.asOf: Mar-26 named holders (FY26 annual report); Jun-26 categories (BSE shareholding pattern via Screener)
ownershipView.intro: The three founders are the promoters, with 6.34% each (19.0% together). The rest of the register is mostly the venture and growth funds that financed the company before the IPO. Because most of them are foreign entities, they sit in the "FII" bucket, which is why foreign holdings look so high (55% at Jun-2026). The six-month lock-in on pre-IPO holders ended on 17-Mar-2026; since then SBI Mutual Fund has been the main buyer and venture funds the main sellers.
ownershipView.source: FY26 annual report (note 14, holders above 5% at 31-Mar-2026); BSE shareholding pattern Jun-2026 via Screener.in
ownershipView.read: **What this means:** the free float is still growing as venture funds exit. Accel cut its stake from 6.1% to 4.8% in the 13-Aug-2026 block deal (SBI Mutual Fund bought ₹428 cr at ₹136); VY Capital and Bessemer also sold. With ~40% still held by pre-IPO investors, supply will keep meeting every rally. The founders own only 19% between them, so they are managers more than controlling owners.

verdicts: Quarterly shareholders' letter with segment P&Ls, contribution margin, NTV by segment, a full reconciliation to Ind AS and free cash flow; InstaHelp unit economics by quarter.
Among the best in Indian internet.
Adjusted EBITDA deducts rent but leaves out ESOP (₹104 cr FY26) and the KSA JV loss; FY25 profit was a ₹211 cr tax credit; ₹60 cr DTA reversed in FY26; ₹151 cr DTA still on the books.
Read profit on the reconciled lines, not the headline.
Core cash is being spent on InstaHelp (₹235 cr loss in FY26, ₹132 cr in Q1FY27 alone) in a subsidy war with venture-funded rivals.
Rational if it wins the category; costly if the war drags on.
Founders paid 33.6x the median employee; 10 cr options (6.4% of shares) outstanding at ₹1; ESOP cost ~₹150 cr a year.
Half independent, with well-known names; auditor rotated from Price Waterhouse to BSR & Co at the 2026 AGM (end of term).
Its model depends on ~79,000 monthly active partners; partner protests in 2021 and the new labour codes (1-2% of turnover for gig-worker welfare) show the regulatory and social risk.
A risk to margins, not to the franchise.

industryView.market: India's home-services market is large but almost entirely offline: Redseer (in the IPO prospectus) puts it at US$59 bn in CY2024, growing 10-11% a year to ~US$97 bn by CY2029, with online platforms under 1% of it. Brokers' estimates are similar: ₹5.1-5.2 lakh crore in FY25 rising to ₹8.4-8.6 lakh crore by FY30, online share 0.8% → 1.3% (Ambit, Mar-2026); online full-stack home services ₹4,100-4,300 cr in FY25, growing 18-22% a year, of which Urban Company has ~65-70% (MOSL, Mar-2026).
industryView.competition: In its core categories Urban Company has no listed or scaled online rival: competition is the local beautician, electrician or cleaner found by word of mouth, plus NoBroker's home services (~2 lakh requests a month, Zivora beauty brand). InstaHelp is different: on-demand house help has drawn venture money. Snabbit raised US$56 mn in Apr-2026 (valued ~US$350 mn) and ran ~1.85 mn orders in Jul-2026; Pronto raised US$45 mn at a ~US$200 mn valuation by May-2026 (~0.95 mn orders a month). InstaHelp is the largest, with >100,000 daily orders by Aug-2026, but all three subsidise orders.

historySource: FY26 annual report, shareholders' letters, exchange and press reports (Inc42, Business Today, Business Standard) dated on or before 30-Sep-2026
moat: Trust and quality control (training, background checks, ratings, warranties)
Average rating 4.79/5 over millions of jobs; 83% of FY26 India NTV from retained users; the model is hard to copy without a decade of operating data.
Local density (supply and demand in each micro-market)
Partner hours up from 59 to 90 a month (FY22-FY26); UC Instant cuts waiting times where density is high; Tier 2 cities growing 36%.
Largest online home-services brand in India (~65-70% of the online full-stack market, MOSL); Native sells half its purifiers to new users.
Contribution margin ~21% of NTV in India; AI-led support savings; but InstaHelp shows rivals can undercut on price with venture money.
Customers and partners can and do go offline after the first booking ("disintermediation"); commissions cap partner loyalty.
critiques: Bulls (UBS, Emkay, Morgan Stanley): a near-monopoly online franchise in a market with <1% online penetration, core margins heading to 9-10% of NTV, International a second profit engine; InstaHelp could be a "Blinkit moment" for home services.

Bears (Ambit, JM Financial, BofA): the core grows ~18-20% a year, not 30%; InstaHelp is a subsidy war with well-funded rivals and weak unit economics (AOV ₹138, loss ₹346 an order); the stock already prices the core at 45-60x FY28E EBITDA.

Our critique: the core is good and getting better, but on our forecasts the group only breaks even in FY29E, and the InstaHelp losses still to come are a real cost, which most bulls ignore or value positively.
